rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_unconstrained-claude-agentic: image_size=512, pixel_spacing=0.3516, n_angles=128, n_det=1024, det_spacing=0.35754, sod=500.0, sdd=1000.0, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.5, train_n=400, val_n=200, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_breast.pt, fd_recon_steps=16, fd_recon_init=noise, fd_recon_init_t=0.7, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=0, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.5, rationale=iter-20 (FINAL): DC-off breast-prior. Architecturally-DISTINCT family for STOP-protocol edge coverage. ONE KNOB init fbp->noise (pure unconditional generation from the prior, ZERO FBP anchor; init_t ignored when init=noise so t starts at 1.0; eta back to 1.0 and steps=16 since full-trajectory generation needs guidance+NFE). PRIOR: the FBP-anchored regime peaks at hr0.271 (init_t0.02) - the entire gain came from lightly denoising the FBP init. HYPOTHESIS: with NO FBP init, the DC-off sampler must reconstruct ENTIRELY from the prior + soft DPS on 128-view sparse data -> hr~0 (cannot match FBP), quantifying that the FBP INIT (not the generative prior per se) is what carries the DC-off variant. This is the honest lower bound: the breast prior as a pure generator (no measurement warm-start) does NOT reconstruct sparse-view breast CT. Completes 20 iters + >=3 distinct families (init_t sweep, eta sweep, NFE, seed-robustness, noise-init).
